summary: The trade ran hugely favorable (up to +44.25pts by t=4m) then reversed sharply, giving back the entire gain and printing negative (-2.75pts) by t=8m -- a genuine round-trip failure, not a normal dip. The tell was the combination of magnitude (full round-trip through the peak into negative territory within 2 minutes) plus persistence: CLIMAX-against, HA-against, and PROPP-against all fired and kept firing across three consecutive frames rather than a single blip. I held through the first pullback (t=7m, still +15.25) since it was still strongly favorable, but bailed the moment px crossed to negative with stacked against-signals. Next time I'd watch for the same signature earlier -- the against-fires actually started at t=7m while price was still positive, so a faster read of stacking against-fires (even while still in profit) could trim the giveback further before it round-trips to negative.
